facts.fact: Kabata (2024) calls the Registration of Persons Act, Cap 107, Kenya's primary identity law, and says the digital identity system was set up by an omnibus amendment to it and not by a stand-alone Act; the paper gives the amendment as 2018, and the year is used.

Kabata (2024) says section 9A of the amended Act establishes the National Integrated Identity Management System, to keep a national population register as the single source of personal information on citizens and resident foreigners and to assign a unique national identification number to every person registered; the paper cites the 2018 amendment, and the year is used.

Kabata (2024) says that with no stand-alone digital identity law the system is anchored on the Huduma Namba regulations, the Registration of Persons (National Integrated Identity Management System) Regulations, 2020, which civil society criticised as creating a substantive system by regulation.
